elements.element: Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it
elements.evidence: "Customer exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer"
"Vendor hereby irrevocably assigns to Customer all right, title, and interest in and to each Deliverable upon creation"
"Vendor retains Vendor Technology in accordance with Section 14.3"; Vendor Technology = "Vendor's pre-existing software, tools, models, templates..."

elements.element: Perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables
elements.evidence: No licence language appears; the redline grants no embedded-IP licence, and the official check flags "preferred embedded-IP licence covers any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables" as failing.

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data
elements.evidence: Clause is silent on Customer Data; only "Vendor Technology does not include Customer Data" appears in definitions, which is not an affirmative retention of rights in this clause.

elements.element: Vendor owns generic tools and know-how
elements.evidence: "Vendor retains Vendor Technology"; know-how excluded from Deliverables per Section 1.4

elements.element: Customer receives perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence
elements.evidence: No licence grant remains after the replacement; the prior "revocable, non-transferable licence" was deleted.

elements.element: Licence rights to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for Customer's business
elements.evidence: Redlined text contains no use, modification, or sublicensing rights.

offending_extra_words: and Vendor hereby irrevocably assigns to Customer all right, title, and interest in and to each Deliverable upon creation
Vendor retains Vendor Technology in accordance with Section 14.3.
reasons: Preferred level is incomplete: the redline flips ownership and adds an assignment but grants no perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to Vendor IP embedded in Deliverables, leaving Customer owning Deliverables that may incorporate Vendor Technology without any licence to it.
Customer Data retention is not addressed in the operative text; the preferred position's express retention of all rights in Customer Data cannot be confirmed from this clause.

Fallback is not satisfied either (and cannot be mixed with preferred): the pre-existing licence sentence was deleted and no perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free use/modify/sublicense licence was inserted.

Minimality fails: the whole clause was rewritten (changed-character ratio 0.718 vs the 0.600 limit) when flipping "Vendor" to "Customer" plus a short assignment insertion would suffice; the added Section 14.3 cross-reference restates protection Vendor already has under Sections 14.3 and 13.2.

Fix: retain more of the original sentence structure, add a concise embedded-IP licence ("Vendor grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in a Deliverable"), and confirm Customer Data rights are expressly retained.
